about: The evangelium of the formulary “16th Sunday after Pentecost” in the 1962 Roman Missal.

seg.tr: At that time, as Jesus was entering the house of a certain ruler of the Pharisees on the sabbath to eat bread, they were watching Him. And behold, a certain man who had dropsy was before Him. And Jesus answered and spoke to those learned in the law and to the Pharisees, saying: Is it lawful to heal on the sabbath? But they kept silent. He, however, took hold of him and healed him, and let him go. And He answered them and said: Which of you will have his donkey or his ox fall into a well, and will not at once pull it out on the sabbath day? And they could not reply to Him about these things. He was also telling a parable to the invited guests, as He noticed how they were choosing the first places at table, saying to them: When you have been invited to a wedding feast, do not take the first seat, lest perhaps someone more honored than you has been invited by him, and he who invited you and him should come and say to you: Make room for this man; and then you would begin with shame to occupy the last seat. But when you have been invited, go, take the last seat, so that when the one who invited you comes, he may tell you: Friend, come up higher. Then there will be glory for you before those who sit at table with you; for everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, and he who humbles himself will be exalted.
